text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Born full term with an uneventful neonatal period. Social history: Patient attends kindergarten. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco smoke.

speaker: Patient
text: All systems review is essentially negative as reported by the mother. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; however, systemic hypertension in a child requires immediate investigation regardless of the migraine history. Are you experiencing any swelling in your face or legs, and have you noticed any changes in your urination frequency or color? I will also request a Renal Ultrasound and Basic Metabolic Panel to evaluate for renal causes of hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I understand your previous doctor suggested migraines, but in a child with systemic hypertension, we must rule out serious secondary causes first. Are you taking any medications like decongestants, birth control, or steroids, and do you have a family history of high blood pressure or kidney disease? Additionally, have you noticed any swelling in your hands, feet, or around your eyes?

REQUEST TEST: Basic_Metabolic_Panel, Electrolytes, Serum_Creatinine, Urinalysis.
REQUEST IMAGES: Renal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: The test results are normal, which effectively rules out renal parenchymal disease. Since secondary causes related to the kidneys appear unlikely, have you been diagnosed with a congenital heart defect like a patent ductus arteriosus, and do you have any symptoms of a heart murmur or shortness of breath during activity? REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram. REQUEST IMAGES: Cardiac_Thumbnails.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Echocardiogram Findings: Narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation. Left ventricular function is normal. Cardiac_Thumbnail: Normal heart size.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta. Given the confirmed narrowing distal to the left subclavian artery and normal renal findings, this is the cause of your systemic hypertension. We will proceed with blood pressure monitoring in both arms and legs to confirm the differential and plan for surgical or catheter-based repair.
